root.label: SFINAE
root.note: An invalid type or expression produced by substitution into a signature removes that template from overload resolution.

children.label: Immediate context
children.note: Only failures in the function type, template parameter types and explicit specifier are soft.

children.label: Signature, not body
children.note: Function bodies are never checked by substitution; errors there are hard.

children.label: Instantiated classes
children.note: An error inside a class template instantiated during substitution is a hard error.

children.label: auto return types
children.note: Asking for a deduced return type instantiates the body, so probing it is a hard error.

children.label: Lambda bodies (C++20)
children.note: A lambda in the signature is not part of the immediate context.

children.label: Substitution order
children.note: Since CWG 1227, substitution runs in lexical order and stops at the first failure.

children.label: Early fail is safe
children.note: A failing return type before a parameter prevents that parameter's instantiations.

children.label: Differing orders
children.note: Redeclarations that substitute in different orders with different results are IFNDR.

children.label: enable_if
children.note: enable_if_t<B, T> names T when B is true and nothing when false, failing substitution.

children.label: Return type
children.note: Simple, but impossible for constructors and conversion functions.

children.label: Defaulted parameter
children.note: Works for constructors but changes arity and function pointer types.

children.label: Template parameter
children.note: Idiomatic; use the non-type form enable_if_t<B, int> = 0.

children.label: Redeclaration trap
children.note: Defaults are not in the signature, so class = enable_if_t<...> twice is a redefinition.

children.label: Class parameter trap
children.note: A non-template member using the class's T in enable_if is a hard error.

children.label: Expression SFINAE
children.note: Since C++11, any invalid expression in the signature counts as a substitution failure.

children.label: decltype(e, void())
children.note: Checks e and yields void; the void() blocks an overloaded comma operator.

children.label: Access checks
children.note: Naming an inaccessible member during substitution is a soft failure.

children.label: Detection idiom
children.note: Partial specialization matching also substitutes, so traits can test validity.

children.label: void_t (C++17)
children.note: Maps any valid types to void so a specialization matches the primary's default.

children.label: is_detected
children.note: Library Fundamentals TS v2 helper; never standardized, superseded by concepts.

children.label: Concepts replace it
children.note: C++20 requires-clauses state conditions directly and also rank overloads.

children.label: No redeclaration trap
children.note: Different constraints make different templates, so overloads just work.

children.label: Same boundary
children.note: Errors inside what a requires-expression instantiates are still hard errors.
